title: An Optimized Protocol for Packaging Pseudotyped Integrase Defective Lentivirus
author: Sengupta, Mukherjee, et al.
materials: cells may be contaminated by mycoplasma; (

steps.title: Prepare producer cells
steps.instruction: Plate HEK293‑TN cells in high‑glucose DMEM supplemented with 10 % FBS, 2 mM GlutaMax, 100 U ml⁻¹ penicillin and 100 U ml⁻¹ streptomycin so that they reach 70–80 % confluency at the time of transfection; keep cells in logarithmic growth phase, avoid >20 passages and test for mycoplasma.

steps.title: Check viral titer expectations
steps.instruction: Expect a lentiviral titer >10⁵ ifu ml⁻¹; if titer is lower, consider (1) cell density outside 70–80 % confluency, (2) poor‑quality endotoxin‑free plasmid DNA, or (3) incorrect plasmid‑to‑reagent ratios.

steps.title: Consider packaging size limit
steps.instruction: Ensure the total insert size does not exceed ~8.5 kb (5′→3′ LTR); note that a 3 kb insert can give titers ≈10‑fold lower than a 1 kb insert, and repeated sequences may impair expression.

steps.title: Prepare DNA‑plasmid mix
steps.instruction: Add 1–1.6 ml serum‑ and antibiotic‑free DMEM to an Eppendorf tube, then add 4.5 µg lentivector DNA and 45 µl packaging plasmid DNA; pipette up‑and‑down 10 times to mix.

steps.title: Prepare transfection mix
steps.instruction: Add 55 µl PureFection reagent to the same tube, vortex for 10 s, and incubate the DNA‑DMEM‑PureFection mixture at room temperature for 15 min.

steps.title: Add transfection mix to cells
steps.instruction: Dispense the transfection mixture drop‑wise onto the producer‑cell dish, swirl gently to distribute evenly, and return the dish to a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator; optionally replace the medium 12–24 h after transfection.

steps.title: Revive fresh HEK293‑TN batch (if needed)
steps.instruction: If cells are over‑confluent, contaminated, or have >20 passages, thaw a new vial of HEK293‑TN cells and culture them to logarithmic growth before repeating the protocol.
